npc.tilda.name: Tilda Ashby
dlg.tilda.first.0: Well, hello there! You must be the new farmer. I'm Tilda, I run the general store.
dlg.tilda.first.1: Seeds, a bit of gossip, and a backpack if you can afford one. Anything else, I can usually find.
dlg.tilda.first.r0_0: The pleasure's mine, [player]. Come by whenever we're open.
dlg.tilda.first.r1_0: Seeds for each season, mostly. Mind the hours: nine to five, and I rest on Sundays.
dlg.tilda.chat1.0: Business is slow before the planting rush. Everyone waits for the first warm day.
dlg.tilda.chat2.0: Wetherell isn't big, but nobody goes hungry. That's more than most places can say.
dlg.tilda.chat3.0: Plant parsnips first, they pay for everything else. Old farmer's trick.
dlg.tilda.rain1.0: Rain is good for crops and terrible for customers. Still, it's nice to listen to.
dlg.tilda.friend1.0: [player]! I saved you the good seat by the window. Don't tell the others.
dlg.tilda.friend2.0: I haven't had a neighbor this easy to talk to in years. It's nice.
dlg.tilda.close1.0: You know, [farm] is turning into the prettiest place in the valley. Everyone says so.
dlg.tilda.close2.0: If you ever need anything, you tell me first. I mean it.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.loved.0: Oh! You remembered! This is wonderful, [player]. Thank you.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.neutral.0: Oh, thank you. That's kind of you.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.disliked.0: Er... thank you. I'm sure someone will want it.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.birthday.0: You remembered my birthday! You've made my whole year.
npc.bram.name: Bram Hollis
dlg.bram.first.1: Bram. Blacksmith. Bring me bars and coin and I'll make your tools better. No haggling.
dlg.bram.first.r1_0: Hand over the tool, the bars and the gold. Two days. Then come and collect it.
dlg.bram.chat3.0: The saloon pours decent cider. Quiet there in the early evening, too.
dlg.bram.rain1.0: Rain on the roof. The forge stays warm, so I'm not complaining.
dlg.bram.friend1.0: You work hard. Good. Keep your tools oiled.
dlg.bram.friend2.0: Hm. Not many people ask how my day went.
dlg.bram.close1.0: Never thought I'd say it, but I look forward to your visits.
dlg.bram.close2.0: Your tools are the best kept in the village. I notice these things.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.loved.0: Hm. Now that's a fine thing. Thank you, [player].
dlg.npc.bram.gift.disliked.0: Hm. What am I supposed to do with this?
dlg.npc.bram.gift.birthday.0: You knew? Hmph. Well. Thank you. Truly.
npc.ione.name: Ione Fairweather
dlg.ione.first.0: Oh! A visitor. I'm Ione. I look after the library.
dlg.ione.first.1: Take your time. Everything here is older than it looks.
dlg.ione.first.r0_0: Almanacs, field notes, a few maps. Anything about the land, really.
dlg.ione.first.r1_0: Another day, perhaps. Wetherell has more stories than readers.
dlg.ione.chat1.0: The almanac says the winter will be gentle. Almanacs have been wrong before.
dlg.ione.chat2.0: On my day off I walk in the forest. The path is lovely when the light is low.
dlg.ione.chat3.0: A good book is a quiet door.
dlg.ione.rain1.0: Rain on the windows is the best reading weather.
dlg.ione.friend1.0: I set a book aside for you. Farming, naturally, but with lovely drawings.
dlg.ione.friend2.0: It's easy to talk to you. That's rarer than you'd think.
dlg.ione.close1.0: I used to read about places like [farm]. It's better in person.
dlg.ione.close2.0: You can come by even when you have nothing to ask. I like the company.
dlg.npc.ione.gift.loved.0: Oh... it's beautiful. Thank you, [player]. Truly.
dlg.npc.ione.gift.liked.0: How lovely. I'll keep it on my desk.
dlg.npc.ione.gift.disliked.0: Oh. Thank you. I... will find a place for it.
dlg.npc.ione.gift.birthday.0: You remembered. Thank you. It's been a long time since anyone did.
dlg.gift.birthday.0: Thank you for remembering my birthday!

letter.welcome.subject: Welcome to Wetherell
letter.welcome.body:
Dear [player],

Welcome to [farm]! The soil is good and there are parsnip seeds in your bag. Till the ground with your hoe, plant, and water every day. Come by the general store when you can: we are open nine to five, every day but Sunday.

Tilda Ashby
letter.tilda_thanks.subject: Thank you for visiting
letter.tilda_thanks.body:
Dear [player],

It was lovely to meet you. Here are a few seeds for your trouble.

Tilda
letter.bram_tools.subject: About your tools
letter.bram_tools.body:
[player],

Good tools last. Take this bar toward your next upgrade.

Bram
letter.ione_recipe.subject: A recipe for you
letter.ione_recipe.body:
Dear [player],

I found this recipe tucked in an old almanac. I think you will make better use of it than I would.

Ione
letter.summer_seeds.subject: Summer seeds are in
letter.summer_seeds.body:
Dear [player],

The summer seeds have arrived at the store. Melons pay well, if you can wait for them.

Tilda

npc.marcus.name: Marcus Dell
dlg.marcus.first.0: Mind the sawdust. Marcus Dell, carpenter.
dlg.marcus.first.1: Need something built, I'm your man. Barns, coops, a greenhouse even.
dlg.marcus.first.r1_0: Anything with a roof and a plan. Bring wood, and gold.
dlg.marcus.chat1.0: A straight board is a happy board.
dlg.marcus.chat2.0: Oak for strength, pine for speed. People always want speed.
dlg.marcus.chat3.0: I measure twice. My father measured three times.
dlg.marcus.rain1.0: Rain makes the roof sing. I like checking what leaks.
dlg.marcus.friend1.0: You've got good hands, [player]. I can tell.
dlg.marcus.friend2.0: Come by Sunday. I'll show you a joint that never fails.
dlg.marcus.close1.0: I built half of this village. [farm] is my favorite job, though.
dlg.marcus.close2.0: A good neighbor is worth more than good lumber.
dlg.npc.marcus.gift.loved.0: Now that is proper craftsmanship. Thank you.
dlg.npc.marcus.gift.neutral.0: Well. Can't say no to a gift. Thanks.
dlg.npc.marcus.gift.disliked.0: Hm. I'll find someone who wants it.
dlg.npc.marcus.gift.birthday.0: My birthday? I'd forgotten. Thank you, truly.
event.marcus_heart2.1: Level as a lake. We make a good team.
event.marcus_heart2.2: Take these. Left over from the big jobs.
event.marcus_heart5.0: I carved this when I was a boy.
event.marcus_heart5.1: Silly, perhaps. But I want you to have it.
npc.odalys.name: Dr. Odalys Penn
dlg.odalys.first.0: Welcome. I'm Dr. Penn, the village doctor.
dlg.odalys.first.1: If you overwork yourself, my door is open. Most farmers do.
dlg.odalys.first.r1_0: Tonics, mostly, for stamina. Come by when you can afford one.
dlg.odalys.chat1.0: Sleep is the best medicine and the cheapest.
dlg.odalys.chat2.0: Everyone thinks they are the exception to rest. They are not.
dlg.odalys.chat3.0: The herbs I use grow right here, if you know where to look.
dlg.odalys.rain1.0: Rainy days bring the sniffles. Keep your feet dry.
dlg.odalys.friend1.0: You look well, [player]. Keep it that way.
dlg.odalys.friend2.0: I could use a hand gathering elderflower. Interested?
dlg.odalys.close1.0: You remind me why I do this work.
dlg.odalys.close2.0: If I ever need a second opinion, I'll ask you about the soil.
dlg.npc.odalys.gift.loved.0: How thoughtful. This will brighten the clinic.
event.odalys_heart2.1: Strong. All that digging pays off.
event.odalys_heart2.2: Here, a tonic. On the house.
event.odalys_heart5.0: I keep a notebook of remedies.
event.odalys_heart5.1: I copied this one out for you.
npc.wren.name: Wren Calloway
dlg.wren.first.0: Well, if it isn't the new farmer! Wren. I run the saloon.
dlg.wren.first.1: Cider, stories, and a seat by the fire. What more could you need?
dlg.wren.first.r0_0: You'd better. I save the good stool for regulars.
dlg.wren.first.r1_0: Oh, sit down. Where do I start...
dlg.wren.chat2.0: I pour a good drink and I keep my ears open. Those are my talents.
dlg.wren.chat3.0: Try the cider. It's the least dangerous thing in here.
dlg.wren.rain1.0: Rain fills the saloon. Business is good, mood is better.
dlg.wren.friend1.0: There's my favorite farmer! Your usual stool's waiting.
dlg.wren.friend2.0: I'll tell you a secret: I hate cooking. Don't tell anyone.
dlg.wren.close1.0: You make this village feel smaller in the best way.
dlg.wren.close2.0: If I ever leave Wetherell, I'd want you to run the place.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.loved.0: Oh, you wonderful menace. This is exactly what I wanted, and I didn't know it until now.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.liked.0: Aren't you sweet? That's going behind the bar for the next dull day.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.disliked.0: Hm. Not my taste, but I'll smile. Between us, I'll regift it to Felix.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.birthday.0: You remembered! Drinks are on me tonight.
event.wren_heart2.0: Slow night, so I'm making a new recipe.
event.wren_heart5.0: Everyone thinks I like the noise.
event.wren_heart5.1: Truth is, I like the people. Thank you for being one.
npc.felix.name: Felix Hartwell
dlg.felix.first.0: Mornin'. Felix. I sell rods and bait and sometimes fish.
dlg.felix.first.1: The tide waits for no one, and neither do I.
dlg.felix.first.r1_0: Beach for the ocean ones, the forest pond for the shy ones.
dlg.felix.chat1.0: Patience is the whole trick. And bait.
dlg.felix.chat2.0: Rain brings eels. They bite like they're angry.
dlg.felix.chat3.0: The moon does strange things to the pond fish.
dlg.felix.rain1.0: Rain's the best time. The fish forget to be careful.
dlg.felix.friend1.0: You're getting the hang of this, [player].
dlg.felix.friend2.0: Take my spot tomorrow. I have a feeling about the tide.
dlg.felix.close1.0: I have fished alone my whole life. This is better.
dlg.felix.close2.0: You've the patience of a heron. Compliment, that.
dlg.npc.felix.gift.loved.0: Now that's a catch of a gift!
dlg.npc.felix.gift.neutral.0: Thanks. I'll find a use for it, even if it's only bait.
dlg.npc.felix.gift.disliked.0: Ah. Fishermen aren't picky, but... no.
event.felix_heart2.1: Feel that pull? That's a good one.
event.felix_heart5.0: Every sailor has a lucky charm.
event.felix_heart5.1: This was mine. Now it's yours.
npc.juno.name: Juno Hale
dlg.juno.first.0: Hi! Juno, Bram's apprentice. Don't mind the soot.
dlg.juno.first.1: I do the fine work. Bram does the loud work.
dlg.juno.first.r0_0: Ha! A neighbor with manners. Welcome.
dlg.juno.first.c1: Can you make me a sword?
dlg.juno.first.r1_0: Bram sells the blades. I'll sharpen your enthusiasm.
dlg.juno.chat1.0: Hammer, tongs, patience. In that order.
dlg.juno.chat2.0: Bram says I talk too much. Bram talks too little.
dlg.juno.chat3.0: Someday I'll make something nobody's seen before.
dlg.juno.rain1.0: Rain on a hot forge: the best sound in the world.
dlg.juno.friend1.0: Look at this, [player]. My first clasp that actually closes!
dlg.juno.friend2.0: You ask good questions. Bram never does.
dlg.juno.close1.0: I always wanted a friend who'd listen about metal.
dlg.juno.close2.0: You're the reason I stayed in Wetherell.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.loved.0: No way! For me? Thank you!
dlg.npc.juno.gift.neutral.0: Thanks! Bram will pretend not to be jealous.
event.juno_heart2.1: See the color? That's the moment.
npc.hazel.name: Hazel Brandt
dlg.hazel.first.0: Oh! Hello. Hazel. I help Ione with the books.
dlg.hazel.first.1: Please don't dog-ear anything. I'll know.
dlg.hazel.first.c1: Do you have a favorite book?
dlg.hazel.first.r1_0: Too many. Ask me again when we're friends.
dlg.hazel.chat1.0: Every book has a smell. Old ones smell like secrets.
dlg.hazel.chat2.0: I read the last chapter first. Don't tell Ione.
dlg.hazel.chat3.0: It's quiet here. That's the point.
dlg.hazel.rain1.0: Rain and a book. There's nothing better.
dlg.hazel.friend1.0: I saved you a new almanac, [player].
dlg.hazel.friend2.0: You're the only person who returns books early.
dlg.hazel.close1.0: I talk to you more than anyone. It's surprising.
dlg.hazel.close2.0: Thank you for coming by. Truly.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.loved.0: Oh. (She goes pink.) This is exactly right. I'll keep it. I'll keep it forever, or until I read it.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.liked.0: That's thoughtful. Thank you. (She tucks it carefully into a pocket she doesn't have.)
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.neutral.0: Thank you. I'll look after it.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.disliked.0: Oh. (She holds it at arm's length.) That's... kind of you. I'll find a place for it. Far away.
event.hazel_heart2.1: A pressed flower, a hundred years old.
event.hazel_heart5.1: It's just a small poem. Don't laugh.
npc.piper.name: Piper Vance
dlg.piper.first.0: Hey! Piper. I play here most evenings.
dlg.piper.first.1: Request anything. I'll probably play something else.
dlg.piper.first.c0: I'd love to hear you play.
dlg.piper.first.r0_0: Then stay for the second set!
dlg.piper.first.r1_0: Fiddle, mostly. And anything with strings that complains.
dlg.piper.chat1.0: Music is just noise that learned manners.
dlg.piper.chat2.0: I wrote a song about parsnips. It's a masterpiece.
dlg.piper.chat3.0: Sunday's the only day I don't play. My fingers beg.
dlg.piper.friend1.0: Sing along tonight, [player]. Don't be shy.
dlg.piper.friend2.0: I wrote a verse about [farm]. Wanna hear?
dlg.piper.close1.0: Playing for you is my favorite thing.
dlg.piper.close2.0: Wetherell needed a song. You're the chorus.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.loved.0: Aw, you shouldn't have! Thank you!
dlg.npc.piper.gift.disliked.0: Haha. Not for me, but thanks for trying.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.birthday.0: You remembered! I'll play your song tonight.
event.piper_heart5.1: I've never played it for anyone else.
npc.dorian.name: Dorian Lake
dlg.dorian.first.1: Dorian. I forage. I lodge with the carpenter. That's all there is.
dlg.dorian.first.r1_0: Truffles, mostly. Whatever the forest forgets.
dlg.dorian.chat2.0: Look under old roots. Everyone looks up.
dlg.dorian.chat3.0: I'd rather talk to a tree than a crowd.
dlg.dorian.rain1.0: Rain's when the mushrooms come out. Good day.
dlg.dorian.friend2.0: Come with me tomorrow. Bring a basket.
dlg.dorian.close1.0: I don't say much. But I'm glad you're here.
dlg.dorian.close2.0: The forest likes you. That's rare.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.neutral.0: Hm. Thanks. I'll put it somewhere safe.
event.dorian_heart2.2: Thanks for being quiet with me.
npc.elara.name: Elara Finch
dlg.elara.first.0: Hello! I'm Elara, the nurse. I do the bandages and the jokes.
dlg.elara.first.1: Dr. Penn does the diagnosing and the frowning.
dlg.elara.first.r0_0: Aw, thank you! You'll fit right in.
dlg.elara.first.c1: Do you ever get a break?
dlg.elara.first.r1_0: Saturdays. And I spend them at the beach.
dlg.elara.chat1.0: The best medicine is a good laugh. And rest. Mostly rest.
dlg.elara.chat2.0: Everyone is braver in the waiting room than they think.
dlg.elara.chat3.0: I knit when it's slow. Don't tell Dr. Penn.
dlg.elara.rain1.0: Rain means sniffles. I'll be busy.
dlg.elara.friend1.0: Hey, [player]! You look better each week.
dlg.elara.friend2.0: I made extra tea. Stay a minute?
dlg.elara.close1.0: You're one of my favorite people to see.
dlg.elara.close2.0: If you ever feel low, come find me.
event.elara_heart2.1: A little bandage for that blister. Don't argue.
event.elara_heart5.1: It's a bit crooked. Wear it anyway.
event.tilda_heart5.0: Sit a moment, [player]. I made too many scones.
event.tilda_heart5.1: I've never had a neighbor who ate my cooking without flinching.
event.bram_heart2.1: Watch the metal. Don't blink. See that? That's heat done right.
event.bram_heart2.2: Now you know something. Don't tell anyone.
event.bram_heart5.1: You're the only one who treats a good tool like a friend. Here.
event.ione_heart2.0: Oh, [player]! Come see what I found.
event.ione_heart2.1: An old chart of the coast. The ink is nearly gone, but look.
event.ione_heart5.0: I wanted to ask you something.
event.ione_heart5.1: Would you walk the beach with me on my next day off? Only if you'd like.
event.ione_heart5.2: Thank you. It means more than you know.

dlg.festival.spring.join.0: The village square is hung with blossoms. Music drifts from the saloon.
dlg.festival.spring.join.r0_0: You dance until your feet ache. It is the happiest evening of the year.
dlg.festival.spring.join.r1_0: You enjoy the evening from the edge of the crowd.
dlg.festival.summer.join.0: Boats and rods line the beach. Felix holds up a chalk board of scores.

content.notes: This game is a cozy farming sim with an optional layer of folk-horror: a secretive village cult, unsettling atmosphere, a creeping sense of dread, and a ritual theme. There is no gore and animals and people are never shown harmed. Mild halves the effects and removes distorted text and explicit ritual scenes. Off removes the layer completely. You can change this at any time in Options.

mythos.dream.mild: You dreamed of tall trees and woke uneasy.
mythos.dream.full: You dreamed of something enormous breathing beneath the roots. You woke with soil under your nails.
mythos.mutation: A crop in your field has grown strangely overnight.

mythos.stone.2: Beneath the moss: the names of those who kept the watch before, every one scratched out but the last.
mythos.stone.2.mild: An old stone listing names, most too worn to read.

mythos.step.1: The birds are a little quieter than they were.
mythos.step.2: The fog lingers a little longer in the mornings.
mythos.step.3: Old dogs refuse to go near the forest path.
mythos.step.4: Milk sours faster. Nobody mentions it.
mythos.step.5: The village lights its lamps earlier.
mythos.step.6: The new moon looks larger than it should.
mythos.step.7: Crops come up in odd shapes.
mythos.step.8: The wind carries a low hum at night.
mythos.step.9: People speak more softly after dark.
mythos.step.10: The moon has a reddish edge when it is full.
mythos.step.12: Keepers are seen in the street at all hours.
mythos.step.13: Shadows lean the wrong way at noon.
mythos.step.14: The fog does not burn off by midday.
mythos.step.16: The hum is a voice, almost.
mythos.step.17: Nobody sleeps through the night anymore.
mythos.step.18: The woods are closer than they were.
dlg.mythos.altar.0: The altar is cold stone, stained dark. Offerings are laid here when the moon is new.
dlg.mythos.altar.c0: Lay the three relics on the stone and speak the sealing.
dlg.mythos.altar.c1: Offer yourself to the Keepers' watch.
dlg.mythos.tilda.clue1.0: She glances at the window before she answers. 'The new moon is a quiet time in Wetherell. Best to be home.'
dlg.mythos.tilda.clue2.0: 'We have always kept something, [player]. My mother, hers. It is only a duty, like the shop.'
dlg.mythos.tilda.clue3.0: Her smile is gone. 'You have been to the clearing. Then you know why we cannot stop.'
dlg.mythos.marcus.clue1.0: 'Do not whistle near the woods at night.' He says it like a joke. He is not joking.
dlg.mythos.marcus.clue2.0: 'I built the altar's frame. The wood I used had to be cut a certain way. It always did.'
dlg.mythos.marcus.clue3.0: 'It sleeps, and it must go on sleeping. I will do what I must. Don't make me do it to you.'
dlg.mythos.odalys.clue1.0: 'You are sleeping badly. Many are, around the new moon. I am not surprised.'
dlg.mythos.odalys.clue2.0: 'There are old remedies in the village, and old duties. I serve both.'
dlg.mythos.odalys.clue3.0: 'If you want to help, come to me when you are certain. Not before.'
dlg.mythos.dorian.clue1.0: He does not look at you. 'The forest knows when the moon is new. So do I.'
dlg.mythos.dorian.clue2.0: 'I carry things into the clearing. Better me than someone who would ask why.'
dlg.mythos.dorian.clue3.0: 'It breathes, you know. The ground. If you stand still long enough.'
dlg.mythos.wren.clue1.0: 'Everyone drinks more at the new moon. Funny, that.' She polishes the same glass again.
dlg.mythos.wren.clue2.0: 'I pour for the Keepers before they go. They tip well. They never come back hungry.'
dlg.mythos.wren.clue3.0: 'Do not follow them. And if you do, do not be seen.'
dlg.mythos.odalys.join.0: 'You have kept our secret and asked nothing. The Keepers could use another pair of steady hands.'
dlg.mythos.odalys.join.1: 'If you stand with us, you will carry what we carry. Think carefully.'
dlg.mythos.odalys.join.r0_0: 'Then listen for the new moon. You will be told where to be.'
dlg.mythos.hazel.clue1.0: 'Have you noticed the dogs? The milk? Someone in this village knows why.'
dlg.mythos.hazel.clue2.0: 'There is a pattern in the records. Four times a year, the same men and women, the same night. I think I know where they go.'
dlg.mythos.hazel.clue3.0: 'There are three things in the wood: a seal, a bell, a thread. If someone put them on the altar and spoke the words in the old book, Nharoth could be put to sleep for good. Not kept. Put.'
dlg.mythos.hazel.sabotage.0: 'If a Keeper were too ill to go, the ritual would fail. A failed ritual lowers nothing. The god would stir the sooner. Decide whether you want that.'
dlg.mythos.hazel.sabotage.r0_0: 'You did not hear that from me.'
dlg.mythos.hazel.sabotage.r1_0: 'You did not hear that from me.'

event.awakening.0: The ground shudders. Every dog in Wetherell begins to howl.
event.awakening.1: Harrow Wood burns without smoke, and then the sky does.
event.awakening.2: The Keepers were right. They always were.

event.resist.1: Something enormous exhales, and does not draw breath again.

event.join.1: You are not afraid. That is the most frightening part.
event.join.2: Each new moon you will walk this path. The village will sleep. So will the god.

dlg.tilda.friend3.0: You're always welcome to sit while I finish the ledger.
dlg.tilda.friend4.0: Marcus says I fuss over you. I say he fusses over beams.
dlg.tilda.close3.0: I used to count the days to closing. Lately I count the days until you stop by.
dlg.tilda.close4.0: Whatever else changes in the valley, [farm] will always be part of it.
dlg.tilda.sea_spring.0: Seed packets are flying off the shelves. I love this week.
dlg.tilda.sea_summer.0: Keep your watering can full. Dry spells are hard on everyone's nerves.
dlg.tilda.sea_fall.0: Pumpkins by the door and jam by the register. Best season to run a shop.
dlg.tilda.sea_winter.0: I keep a pot warming in the back. Customers stay longer and spend less. Worth it.
dlg.tilda.rain2.0: Rain taps the window and the register stays quiet. Perfect weather for tea.
dlg.bram.friend3.0: Juno finished a clasp today. It closes. Don't tell her I said so.
dlg.bram.friend4.0: A tool keeps what you give it. Care, mostly.
dlg.bram.close3.0: Juno talks about you. I don't mind.
dlg.bram.close4.0: I make things to last. Same goes for friends, I suppose.
dlg.bram.sea_spring.0: Ground's loosening. Hinges and hoes come in all week.
dlg.bram.sea_summer.0: Forge in summer. Don't ask how it feels.
dlg.bram.sea_fall.0: Axes and scythes. Harvest keeps me busy.
dlg.bram.sea_winter.0: Cold metal bites. Warm metal listens. That's the whole trade.
dlg.bram.rain2.0: Rain hisses on the chimney. Sounds like the forge breathing.
dlg.ione.friend3.0: Hazel has taken to reading aloud to the cat. We don't have a cat.
dlg.ione.friend4.0: If you want a recommendation, I'm much more useful than the card catalog.
dlg.ione.close3.0: I put your name on the new shelf. The one for people who finish things.
dlg.ione.close4.0: The library is quieter than it was. Yet I don't feel alone in it anymore.
dlg.ione.sea_spring.0: Spring cleaning starts at the top shelf. Dust has opinions.
dlg.ione.sea_summer.0: Windows open, pages curl. A small price for the breeze.
dlg.ione.sea_fall.0: The new almanacs arrive. I smell each one. Hazel says that's strange.
dlg.ione.sea_winter.0: Long nights, longer books. This is our season.
dlg.ione.rain2.0: Rain on the glass, a lamp lit, a good chapter. Please don't speak to me.
dlg.marcus.friend3.0: Dorian lodges with me. I barely notice him. Excellent tenant.
dlg.marcus.friend4.0: A good nail is worth three bad ones. That's my philosophy.
dlg.marcus.close3.0: Come here, I'll show you how this joint works. Patience, mostly.
dlg.marcus.close4.0: Houses are easy. Neighbors are the hard part. You're proof it can go well.
dlg.marcus.sea_spring.0: Barn season. Everyone wants a roof before the rain stops.
dlg.marcus.sea_summer.0: Dry wood and long days. I get more done in summer than any other time.
dlg.marcus.sea_fall.0: Fall is for patching. Every wall has a secret hole.
dlg.marcus.sea_winter.0: Cold hands, careful cuts. I plane indoors and think about spring.
dlg.marcus.rain2.0: Rain on the shingles. That's how you find out who did their job.
dlg.odalys.friend3.0: Elara thinks I'm too stern. I think she's too easily amused. We balance.
dlg.odalys.friend4.0: Most patients lie about how much they rest. You haven't. I noticed.
dlg.odalys.close3.0: I don't say it often: it helps knowing someone sensible lives nearby.
dlg.odalys.close4.0: If the day goes badly, the clinic kettle is on. Come as you are.
dlg.odalys.sea_spring.0: Spring fever is real, and so is pollen. I get both.
dlg.odalys.sea_summer.0: Sunburn and heat exhaustion. Hats, everyone. Hats.
dlg.odalys.sea_fall.0: Harvest strains: backs, wrists, tempers. I stock liniment.
dlg.odalys.sea_winter.0: Colds, coughs and chilblains. Keep your socks dry.
dlg.odalys.rain2.0: Wet weather means wet feet. Dry socks are medicine.
dlg.wren.friend3.0: Piper's practicing a new tune. Mostly it's the old tune.
dlg.wren.friend4.0: I keep a tab for everyone. Yours is mostly smiles.
dlg.wren.close3.0: You're the only customer who asks how I am. I don't know what to do with that.
dlg.wren.close4.0: Tilda says I give things away. She's right. Only to people who deserve it.
dlg.wren.sea_spring.0: Spring thaw, spring thirst. Everyone wants something fresh.
dlg.wren.sea_summer.0: Cold cider and open windows. Summer nights run long here.
dlg.wren.sea_fall.0: Harvest night is my favorite. Every farmer arrives with a story.
dlg.wren.sea_winter.0: The fire does half my work in winter. I just pour.
dlg.wren.rain2.0: Rain brings the whole village in. The place smells of wet wool and good cider.
dlg.felix.friend3.0: I mark the good spots in my head. Ask nicely and I might tell you.
dlg.felix.friend4.0: A loose line means a restless fish. Or a bad knot. Usually the knot.
dlg.felix.close3.0: People think fishing is quiet. It's company without the talking. You get it.
dlg.felix.close4.0: Strange how quickly a person becomes part of the tide. You have.
dlg.felix.sea_spring.0: Spring runs bring the silver fish. Early start, good luck.
dlg.felix.sea_summer.0: Summer is for the beach and the long evening cast.
dlg.felix.sea_fall.0: Fall tide, fat fish. Mind your cold hands.
dlg.felix.sea_winter.0: Ice makes the pond fish sleepy. Patience, patience.
dlg.felix.rain2.0: Rain on the water makes a thousand tiny drums. The fish love it.
dlg.juno.friend3.0: Bram let me finish a whole latch alone. Don't tell him I cheered.
dlg.juno.friend4.0: I keep a sketchbook of ideas. Ask nicely and I might show you.
dlg.juno.close3.0: See the pattern in this blade? I draw it first, then hammer it out.
dlg.juno.close4.0: You listen the way metal listens. Weird compliment, I know.
dlg.juno.sea_spring.0: New season, new orders. Hinges, hinges, hinges.
dlg.juno.sea_summer.0: The forge is a sauna. I've made friends with the water bucket.
dlg.juno.sea_fall.0: Harvest tools all week. I'm learning scythes.
dlg.juno.sea_winter.0: Winter's cozy at the forge. Everyone suddenly needs repairs.
dlg.juno.rain2.0: Rain on the roof, glow on the forge. This is my favorite weather.
dlg.hazel.friend3.0: Ione pretends not to hear me humming.
dlg.hazel.friend4.0: If you want a cozy read, ask me. I keep a list.
dlg.hazel.close3.0: I keep a list of books I'd recommend to you specifically. It's long.
dlg.hazel.close4.0: I'm braver in this library than anywhere. You made me braver elsewhere too.
dlg.hazel.sea_spring.0: The spring catalog is out. Everything smells of fresh paper.
dlg.hazel.sea_summer.0: It's cool in here. Quiet. I never want to leave.
dlg.hazel.sea_fall.0: Leaves on the windowsill. They make the best bookmarks.
dlg.hazel.sea_winter.0: Snow outside, tea inside, book in hand. I'm hardly ever unhappy.
dlg.hazel.rain2.0: Rain makes the library cozier. I'll make tea if you stay.
dlg.piper.friend3.0: Wren says I play too loud. Wren is wrong.
dlg.piper.friend4.0: I tune by ear. Which means I tune by guess.
dlg.piper.close3.0: I'm writing something new. It's about a farm on the edge of the village. Guess which.
dlg.piper.close4.0: Every musician needs one person who hears the whole song. Thanks.
dlg.piper.sea_spring.0: Spring tunes are bouncy. Everyone smiles at a bouncy tune.
dlg.piper.sea_summer.0: Long evenings, open doors. Half the crowd is outside.
dlg.piper.sea_fall.0: Harvest songs write themselves. Mostly about pumpkins.
dlg.piper.sea_winter.0: Winter ballads. The slower the better. The fire keeps time.
dlg.piper.rain2.0: Rain on the roof is a free drummer. I never say no.
dlg.dorian.friend3.0: Marcus snores. The forest never does.
dlg.dorian.close3.0: There's a spot where the light comes through just so. You'd like it.
dlg.dorian.close4.0: Most people see trees. You see where they're going. I noticed.
dlg.dorian.sea_spring.0: First shoots under the leaf litter. Tread softly.
dlg.dorian.sea_summer.0: Too hot for truffles. Berries, though.
dlg.dorian.sea_winter.0: Quiet woods. Frost on every branch. I stay out longer than I should.
dlg.dorian.rain2.0: Mushrooms drink the rain. So do I, sometimes.
dlg.elara.friend3.0: Dr. Penn pretended not to laugh at my joke today. I counted it a win.
dlg.elara.friend4.0: I'm learning a scarf pattern. It's mostly knots.
dlg.elara.close3.0: On bad days I think of the people who stop by. You're on that list.
dlg.elara.close4.0: It means a lot, having a friend who isn't a patient.
dlg.elara.sea_spring.0: Spring means allergies. I carry tissues the way other people carry keys.
dlg.elara.sea_summer.0: Beach Saturdays are the best. I always come back sunburned.
dlg.elara.sea_fall.0: Harvest sprains, mostly. Wrists and backs.
dlg.elara.sea_winter.0: Hot tea, thick socks, knitting. Winter's my season.
dlg.elara.rain2.0: Rain means a full waiting room. And a lot of cookies.
dlg.odalys.friend2.r0: Wonderful. I gathered a few already. Take these, the rest are for the clinic.
dlg.odalys.friend2.r1: Of course. The elderflower isn't going anywhere.
dlg.odalys.friend2b.0: The elderflower dried beautifully. Thank you for the help, [player].
dlg.piper.friend2.r0: Ahem. 'A farm on the edge, with parsnips for pride...' Okay, it needs work.
dlg.piper.friend2.r1: Shy audiences are the best. I'll wait.
dlg.piper.friend2b.0: I've got a second verse now. Come back when you're ready for the sequel.
dlg.elara.friend2.r0: Wonderful! Sit. Sugar? I'll pretend I don't see you taking two.
dlg.elara.friend2.r1: Next time, then. The kettle never really goes cold.
dlg.elara.friend2b.0: I've started leaving a second cup out. Just in case.
dlg.marcus.friend2.r0: Bring your own mallet. And patience.
dlg.marcus.friend2b.0: There's still sawdust on my sleeve from Sunday. Good afternoon, that was.
dlg.felix.friend2.r0: Bait's on me. Cast long and wait.
dlg.felix.friend2.r1: Suit yourself. The tide is patient.
dlg.felix.friend2b.0: Did you take my spot? The tide's still good. Mind the third rock.
dlg.dorian.friend2.r0: Early, then. Quietly. Here, start your basket.
dlg.dorian.friend2b.0: That basket was heavy on the way back. Good heavy.
dlg.hazel.book.0: You asked about my favorite book. It's about a lighthouse keeper who writes letters to the sea.
dlg.hazel.book.1: I've read it eleven times. The sea never writes back. That's the point.
dlg.wren.first.r1_1: Tilda hides the best jam. Juno burned another clasp. And Bram smiled once. Once. Don't repeat it.
dlg.tilda.chat4.0: Ask me anything about the village. I know everyone's order.
dlg.ione.chat4.0: People think a library is silent. It's only waiting.
dlg.wren.chat4.0: Cider cures most things. For the rest, I pour a second glass.
dlg.bram.chat4.0: Measure once, strike true. Everything else is noise.

menu.prompt.wren: Another round? Go on, ask me anything.
menu.prompt.hazel: (She looks up from her book.) Yes?
menu.social_prompt: What did you have in mind?
dlg.social.wren.joke.great.0: Ha! Oh, that's wonderful. I'm stealing that. Between us, I'll say it's mine.
dlg.social.wren.joke.good.0: Ha! Good one. Sit. You've earned a cider.
dlg.social.wren.joke.flop.0: ...Oh! That was the punchline? Marvelous. Let me improve it for you.
dlg.social.wren.compliment.great.0: Careful. I'll be insufferable by closing time.
dlg.social.wren.compliment.good.0: Well. Aren't you sweet. The stool is yours.
dlg.social.wren.compliment.flop.0: Flattery? Suspicious. What do you want? ...Oh. Nothing. Thank you.
dlg.social.wren.advice.great.0: Advice? Pull up the stool. First: never trust a quiet cider. Second: sit by the fire.
dlg.social.wren.advice.good.0: My advice? Say yes to the second drink. And no to the third.
dlg.social.wren.advice.flop.0: Advice? Me? I run a bar. Mostly I improvise. Thank you anyway.
dlg.social.wren.tease.great.0: Oh, you wicked thing! I love it. Do it again.
dlg.social.wren.tease.flop.0: Hm. Funny. I'll remember that when you order.
dlg.social.hazel.joke.great.0: (She laughs, then covers her mouth.) That was good. I'm writing it down.
dlg.social.hazel.joke.good.0: Ha. Shh... no, it's fine. That was funny.
dlg.social.hazel.joke.flop.0: Is that a joke? (She checks the page.) Oh. Oh! Ha. Sorry. Slow reader.
dlg.social.hazel.compliment.great.0: Oh. (She goes pink.) I... thank you. Truly. I'll remember that.
dlg.social.hazel.compliment.flop.0: Oh. Er. (She hides behind a book.) Thank you. Please stop being nice for a moment.
dlg.social.hazel.advice.great.0: Oh. You want a recommendation? I have a list. (She does.) Start short. Then something sad.
dlg.social.hazel.advice.good.0: Hm. Let me think. Read slowly. Stay curious.
dlg.social.hazel.advice.flop.0: Advice? I shelve books. (She looks alarmed.) Ask Ione.
dlg.social.hazel.tease.great.0: (A real smile.) That was fair. And annoying. Well done.
dlg.social.hazel.tease.good.0: Hm. That was funny. Don't do it again.
dlg.social.hazel.tease.flop.0: (She goes very still.) I'm going to alphabetize something now.
dlg.social.bram.compliment.good.0: Hm. Fine. Keep your tools oiled.
dlg.social.bram.compliment.flop.0: ...Hm. (He scowls at the anvil.) No need for that.
dlg.social.bram.advice.great.0: Advice. Hm. Heat it slowly. Strike once, strike true. Then leave it alone.
dlg.social.bram.advice.good.0: Hm. Oil your tools. That's the whole secret.
dlg.social.bram.tease.flop.0: (He looks at you. Then at the anvil. Then at you.) Hm. Busy.
topic.hazel.library: Ask about working at the library
dlg.wren.topic.gossip.0: Oh, sit, sit. Now, between us...
dlg.wren.topic.gossip.1: {Tilda hides the best jam.|Juno burned another clasp.|Piper wrote a song about parsnips. Again.|Bram said four words yesterday. Four!}
dlg.wren.topic.gossip.2: Of course, it improves with age. Ask me again Thursday.
dlg.wren.topic.stool.0: The good stool? Third from the fire. Nobody sits there.
dlg.wren.topic.stool.1: Not a rule. A feeling. A very polite feeling.
dlg.wren.topic.stool.2: ...It's yours, by the way. Don't tell Felix.
dlg.hazel.topic.recommendation.1: {if farm:animals>=1}There's a book about a shepherd who talked to her sheep. They never answered. She didn't mind.{else}{if farm:crops>=3}There's a book about a gardener who counted her seeds until the garden counted back.{else}There's a book about a very small field and a very large sky.{/if}{/if}
dlg.hazel.topic.recommendation.2: I'll set it aside. (I already have.)
dlg.hazel.topic.library.0: I shelve. I mend spines. I listen to Ione hum.
dlg.hazel.topic.library.1: {It's quiet.|It's mostly quiet.|It is, on a good day, silent.} I like that.
dlg.bram.topic.forge.1: Heat it until it's honest. Then hit it.
dlg.bram.topic.tools.1: {if has:resource.copperbar>=1}You carry copper. Good. Bring it here.{else}Bring bars and coin. Two days. No haggling.{/if}
dlg.social.joke.great.0: Ha! Oh, that's a good one. I'm going to repeat that.
dlg.social.joke.flop.0: ...Was that a joke? Oh! Ha. Give me a second.
dlg.social.compliment.great.0: Oh, you're too kind. That honestly made my day.
dlg.social.compliment.good.0: That's kind of you to say.
dlg.social.compliment.flop.0: Oh. Er... thank you. That was unexpected.
dlg.social.advice.great.0: You want my advice? Gladly. Take your time, and trust your gut.
dlg.social.advice.good.0: My advice? Slow down and enjoy it.
dlg.social.advice.flop.0: Advice? Oh. I'm the wrong person to ask. Truly.
dlg.social.tease.great.0: Ha! Oh, you're cheeky. I like it.
dlg.social.tease.flop.0: Hm. I'll pretend I didn't hear that.
