dlg.bram.spring.1.0: Hm. Ground's soft. Hoes and hinges all week.
dlg.bram.spring.2.0: Spring. Every plow in the village wants me at once.
dlg.bram.spring.3.0: Hm. First thaw. Old tools show their cracks.
dlg.bram.spring.4.0: Someone brought me a hoe with a bent handle and a long story. I fixed the hoe.
dlg.bram.spring.5.0: Spring means mud. Mud means rust. Rust means work.
dlg.bram.spring.6.0: Hm. Juno talked through all of March. I learned the names of her seven favorite hammers.
dlg.bram.summer.2.0: Hm. Hot. I wear less. The anvil doesn't care.
dlg.bram.summer.3.0: Summer work is hinges and hooks. Quick jobs.
dlg.bram.summer.4.0: I keep a bucket by the door. Juno calls it the swimming pool. I call it the bucket.
dlg.bram.summer.5.0: Long days. The glow of the forge looks small at noon.
dlg.bram.summer.6.0: Hm. Fished once. Caught nothing. Felix said it was a good start.
dlg.bram.fall.1.0: Scythes. Axes. Hooks. Harvest keeps me busy.
dlg.bram.fall.2.0: Hm. Cool air. Good for the metal.
dlg.bram.fall.3.0: Fall is when everyone remembers the fall of their tools.
dlg.bram.fall.4.0: Birthday's in fall. I don't bring it up.
dlg.bram.fall.5.0: Hm. Leaves on the forge roof. They hiss when they land.
dlg.bram.fall.6.0: Fall's my best season. Cold outside. Warm inside. Quiet in between.
dlg.bram.winter.1.0: Winter. The forge is the best seat in the village.
dlg.bram.winter.2.0: Cold metal bites. Warm metal listens.
dlg.bram.winter.3.0: Hm. People come in to warm up. Some order a nail.
dlg.bram.winter.4.0: Snow on the roof. Fire in the belly. That's winter.
dlg.bram.winter.5.0: Winter work is slow. Slow work is good work.
dlg.bram.winter.6.0: Hm. I write letters in winter. Most I don't send.
dlg.bram.mon.1.0: Hm. Monday's my day off. I'm here anyway.
dlg.bram.mon.2.0: Closed Mondays. Doesn't mean I'm not working.
dlg.bram.tue.1.0: Tuesday. Wren's day off. The village is slightly less loud.
dlg.bram.tue.2.0: Hm. Quiet day. Plows and pans.
dlg.bram.wed.1.0: Wednesday. Marcus is closed. We sit on a bench. In silence. It's good.
dlg.bram.thu.1.0: Hm. Thursday. Felix's day off. His hooks are all mine.
dlg.bram.thu.2.0: Thursdays I sharpen. Everything. Even the spoons.
dlg.bram.fri.1.0: Friday. Everyone wants their tool done by Saturday.
dlg.bram.fri.2.0: Hm. Friday means orders. Orders mean noise. I accept noise.
dlg.bram.sat.1.0: Saturday. The market's loud. The forge isn't.
dlg.bram.sat.2.0: Hm. Saturday. Juno's cheerful. I allow it.
dlg.bram.sun.1.0: Sunday. I fix things nobody asked me to fix.
dlg.bram.sun.2.0: Hm. Slow Sunday. Good iron doesn't hurry.
dlg.bram.sunny.1.0: Hm. Bright. Hot inside. Hotter outside.
dlg.bram.sunny.2.0: Good weather. Bad for business. Everyone's outside.
dlg.bram.sunny.3.0: Hm. Sun on the anvil. It shines. It means nothing.
dlg.bram.rain.3.0: Rain on the roof. Forge stays warm. I'm content.
dlg.bram.rain.4.0: Hm. Rain. Everyone brings in tools to dry. I'm a laundry.
dlg.bram.storm.1.0: Storm. Quench barrel's overflowing. I'll allow it.
dlg.bram.storm.2.0: Hm. Thunder. The anvil rings back. They know each other.
dlg.bram.storm.3.0: Lightning's loud. The forge is louder. I win.
dlg.bram.snow.1.0: Snow. The forge glows in it. It looks warm.
dlg.bram.snow.2.0: Hm. Snow on the sill. I leave the door open a crack. Pretty.
dlg.bram.snow.3.0: Snow muffles everything. Even the hammer. I like it.
dlg.bram.wind.1.0: Wind. The door argues. I let it.
dlg.bram.wind.2.0: Hm. Wind blows ash everywhere. I'll be gray for days.
dlg.bram.wind.3.0: Windy. The forge roars. Good for the fire. Bad for my hat.
dlg.bram.morning.1.0: Early. The fire needs coaxing. So do I.
dlg.bram.morning.2.0: Hm. Morning. First heat of the day. First good thought.
dlg.bram.morning.3.0: Before opening. Just me and the iron.
dlg.bram.midday.1.0: Hm. Midday. Peak heat. Peak noise.
dlg.bram.midday.2.0: Busy. Don't stand in the sparks.
dlg.bram.midday.3.0: Afternoon. The best iron gets made now.
dlg.bram.evening.1.0: Closing soon. The fire's low. So's my mood. In a good way.
dlg.bram.evening.2.0: Hm. Evening. I clean up. Then I sit. That's my day.
dlg.bram.evening.3.0: Last job of the day. Always the hard one.
dlg.bram.late.1.0: Late. The anvil's still warm. So is the bench.
dlg.bram.late.2.0: Hm. Late. I should sleep. The iron says otherwise.
dlg.bram.here.1.0: Don't touch that. It's hot. Everything's hot.
dlg.bram.here.2.0: Hm. Careful. The floor's got opinions.
dlg.bram.here.3.0: Juno labeled every tool on the wall. Some labels are insults. I left them.
dlg.bram.fr.2.0: You oil your tools. I noticed.
dlg.bram.fr.3.0: Juno says I'm nicer around you. I said I'm not. She laughed.
dlg.bram.fr.4.0: Wren bet I'd say four words to you today. Hm. That was five.
dlg.bram.fr.5.0: I made you something. It's not ready. It might never be.
dlg.bram.fr.6.0: Hm. Good to see you. Don't tell anyone I said so.
dlg.bram.fr.7.0: Marcus asked about you. I said you're all right. He nodded. That's a lot.
dlg.bram.fr.8.0: I moved the stool so you could sit by the fire. It was in the way anyway.
dlg.bram.cl.1.0: Hm. I look forward to your visits. There. I said it.
dlg.bram.cl.2.0: I used to work alone. This is better. Don't make me say it twice.
dlg.bram.cl.3.0: You talk to me like I'm a person. I try to do the same.
dlg.bram.cl.5.0: Juno's proud of you. So am I. She said it first.
dlg.bram.cl.6.0: I told Wren you're a decent sort. She told everyone. I'm not speaking to Wren.
dlg.bram.cl.7.0: Hm. Come back tomorrow. I'll have something.
dlg.bram.cl.8.0: Your tools are the best kept in the village. I'm not surprised.
dlg.bram.co.1.0: ...Hm. A good friend is a good tool. Hard to find. Harder to keep. You, I'm keeping.
dlg.bram.co.2.0: I made a lot of things. Few I'm proud of. You're on that list.
dlg.bram.co.3.0: Hm. The forge is warm. With you in it, it's warmer.
dlg.bram.co.4.0: If I wrote you a letter, it'd be three words. I'd send it. That's the difference.
dlg.bram.co.5.0: I used to count the days alone. I stopped.
dlg.bram.co.6.0: Hm. Thank you, [player]. For everything. That's the whole speech.
dlg.bram.co.7.0: I don't say much. You never needed me to.
dlg.bram.co.8.0: ...Hm. The anvil has one mark I never fixed. It's from the day you walked in.
dlg.bram.lonely.1.0: Hm. Quiet. Too quiet. Juno was louder than usual to fill it.
dlg.bram.lonely.2.0: You were gone. I noticed. The forge noticed.
dlg.bram.tired.1.0: Long night. The iron kept me up.
dlg.bram.tired.2.0: Hm. Tired. Don't tell Juno. She'll make it a thing.
dlg.bram.delighted.1.0: ...Hm. Good day. A fine pour. A true edge. Good.
dlg.bram.delighted.2.0: Hm. Made something right. Don't ask what. Just look at it.
dlg.bram.mischief.1.0: Hm. I put a rubber chicken on Juno's anvil. Wren swore it was an accident.
dlg.bram.mischief.2.0: Hm. I said something funny. Nobody noticed. I'm pleased.
dlg.bram.worried.1.0: Hm. A blade I made today won't hold. I'll start again.
dlg.bram.farm.1.0: Hm. Your field's coming along. Your hoe will need me soon.
dlg.bram.farm.2.0: Plenty of plants. Plenty of tools to break. Good for business.
dlg.bram.farm.3.0: Animals. They'll need fences. Fences need nails. Nails are me.
dlg.bram.farm.4.0: Hm. Do the chickens like you? They'd better.
dlg.bram.fest.1.0: Festival soon. I'll bring a cookie. One.
dlg.bram.fest.2.0: Hm. Festival. Juno's making me go. I'll stand near the food.
dlg.bram.fest.3.0: Festival today. I put on a clean shirt. Don't make a fuss.
dlg.bram.bday.1.0: Hm. My birthday's close. No fuss. No cake. Maybe cake.
dlg.bram.bday.2.0: Three days. I'll be thirty-something. Hm. I stopped counting.
dlg.bram.bday.3.0: Hm. It's today. Someone told. I know who. Wren.
dlg.bram.bday.4.0: Juno's birthday is close. I made her a tool. She'll cry. I'll pretend not to notice.
dlg.bram.bday.5.0: Wren's birthday. I'll bring a cider. And four words. She'll pick which.
dlg.bram.rare.1.0: Rocks are honest. Weather isn't. Wren isn't either.
dlg.bram.rare.2.0: Hm. I don't talk much. Juno talks for both. She's done it so long I'm in debt.
dlg.bram.rare.3.0: Hm. A good tool doesn't hurry. A good friend doesn't either.
dlg.bram.rare.4.0: Hm. (He looks at the anvil, then at you.) That's the longest I've held a conversation. Don't spread it.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.forage.truffle.0: ...Hm. A truffle. Where'd you find it? Never mind. Thank you.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.forage.mushroom.0: Hm. Good mushroom. I'll have it with supper. Thank you, [player].
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.food.roasted_root: Roasted roots. Hm. Warm. Plain. Right. Thank you.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.resource.copperba: Hm. Copper. Clean pour. You've got an eye.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.forage.hazelnut.0: Hazelnut. Small. Good. I'll eat it slowly.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.crop.potato.0: A potato. Honest. Hm. I'll take it.
A dandelion. Hm. I don't know what to do with it. (He sets it on the anvil.) It looks wrong there.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.crop.kale.0: Kale. Hm. I'll give it to Juno. She'll eat anything.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.fish.pufferfish.0: A pufferfish. It's looking at me. Hm. I'll feed it to someone else.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.cat.Fish.0: Fish. Hm. Felix's department. I'll walk it over.
Hm. Iron. I make iron. This is a very kind insult.
Gold. Hm. Too soft for work. Too pretty to ignore. Thank you.
Ore. Hm. That's the beginning of something. I'll finish it.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.resource.copperor: Copper ore. Hm. Green's good. Means it's honest.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.resource.stone.0: A rock. Hm. It's a good rock. I'll put it on the shelf. It's a friend.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.resource.wood.0: Wood. Hm. For the fire. Marcus would cry at that. I won't tell him.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.resource.slime.0: Slime. ...Hm. No. (He sets it far away.) Thank you for the thought.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.resource.bone.0: A bone. Hm. Strong. Light. A good handle, in a different life.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.artisan.wine.0: Wine. Hm. Wren would approve. I'll save it.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.crop.pumpkin.0: A pumpkin. Hm. Big. I'll carve a hammer on it.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.product.egg.0: An egg. Hm. Smaller than my hammer. Better too.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.item.food.salad.0: Salad. Hm. I'll eat it. Standing up. Quickly.
dlg.npc.bram.gift.repeat.0: Hm. Again. ...Thanks. I still have the first one. It's good.
dlg.hazel.spring.1.0: Spring catalog week. Every book gets dusted and every dust cloud gets a name.
dlg.hazel.spring.2.0: The reading nook warms up first. I've started to leave a window open. (For the pages.)
dlg.hazel.spring.3.0: The first butterfly this year landed on a dictionary. I took it as a review.
dlg.hazel.spring.4.0: Everyone borrows gardening books in spring. Nobody returns them until fall. (Mud is a bookmark.)
dlg.hazel.spring.5.0: I logged the first robin on the second of the season. It's in the margins of the almanac.
dlg.hazel.spring.6.0: Spring smells like damp paper and possibility. I hold one of them closer.
dlg.hazel.summer.1.0: The library is the coolest room in Wetherell. This is not public information.
dlg.hazel.summer.2.0: Summer readers come in sunburned and leave educated. It's a fair trade.
dlg.hazel.summer.3.0: A moth got into the poetry shelf. I've decided it's a critic.
dlg.hazel.summer.4.0: Someone returned a book with sand in it. I now own a very small beach.
dlg.hazel.summer.5.0: Long evenings mean longer chapters. I read until the lamp gives up.
dlg.hazel.summer.6.0: I counted eleven fireflies from the back steps. (Wren says forty-one. She's improved them.)
dlg.hazel.fall.1.0: Leaves on the windowsill. They make the best bookmarks, and the worst housekeeping.
dlg.hazel.fall.2.0: New almanacs arrive in fall. Ione smells each one. I pretend not to notice.
dlg.hazel.fall.3.0: My birthday is in fall. I told no one. Ione told everyone.
dlg.hazel.fall.4.0: Rain, a lamp, and a shelf of unread things. This is the season I was made for.
dlg.hazel.fall.5.0: Every fall I reread the same book. It never ends the same. (I do.)
dlg.hazel.fall.6.0: Harvest brings the crowd. I hide behind the shelves and do a head count by shoes.
dlg.hazel.winter.1.0: Winter is reading season. I turn into a very quiet furnace.
dlg.hazel.winter.2.0: Snow muffles the street, and the library hums a little louder. (Pipes. Not ghosts.)
dlg.hazel.winter.3.0: Ione brings tea in winter. I've stopped pretending I don't want it.
dlg.hazel.winter.4.0: A lamp in a snowed-in window. I could stare at that all day. Some days I do.
dlg.hazel.winter.5.0: The longest nights are for the longest books. I have a list.
dlg.hazel.winter.6.0: I wrote a small poem about the first frost. It has two good lines. I'm told that's generous.
dlg.hazel.mon.1.0: Monday. The returns box is heavy. The mood is heavier.
dlg.hazel.mon.2.0: Mondays I reshelve. It's an act of quiet defiance against chaos.
dlg.hazel.tue.1.0: Tuesday is stamp day. Eleven hundred stamps. I find it soothing.
dlg.hazel.tue.2.0: Tuesdays are slow. The shelves finally exhale.
dlg.hazel.wed.1.0: Wednesday, the middle of the week. Most readers hide in the middle of books.
dlg.hazel.wed.2.0: Wednesdays I mend spines. A spine only needs a little glue and an apology.
dlg.hazel.thu.1.0: Thursday. Someone returns something overdue every Thursday. I've come to respect the rhythm.
dlg.hazel.thu.2.0: Thursdays the nook is warm and nobody comes. I keep it for myself. (And now you.)
dlg.hazel.fri.1.0: Friday. The weekend readers arrive early, with plans and a distressing lack of bookmarks.
dlg.hazel.fri.2.0: I read one chapter aloud to myself every Friday. The shelves are a forgiving audience.
dlg.hazel.sat.1.0: Saturday's the library's day off. I'm only here out of habit. (It's a good habit.)
dlg.hazel.sat.2.0: Saturdays I walk. A book is a good place to leave. A path is a better place to come back from.
dlg.hazel.sun.1.0: Sunday. The quietest day, which is saying something.
dlg.hazel.sun.2.0: Sundays I read in the garden. Ink and sunshine do not agree. I try anyway.
dlg.hazel.sunny.1.0: A bright day. The dust looks like tiny, patient snow.
dlg.hazel.sunny.2.0: Sun on the shelves fades the spines. I keep the curtains half drawn. (Books have feelings.)
dlg.hazel.sunny.3.0: Good light for reading. Terrible light for hiding. I'll manage.
dlg.hazel.rain.3.0: Rain on the roof, a lamp, and a book I've read eleven times. (Twelve soon.)
dlg.hazel.rain.4.0: Rainy days fill the library with strangers. I give them blankets and a very small smile.
dlg.hazel.storm.1.0: Thunder. The windows hum. I pull the books a little closer, in case they're nervous.
dlg.hazel.storm.2.0: A storm like this is a good excuse to stay put and finish a chapter. Several chapters.
dlg.hazel.storm.3.0: I wrote the storm down in the almanac margin. Time, direction, volume. (Volume: extreme.)
dlg.hazel.snow.1.0: Snow. The library looks like it's been tucked in.
dlg.hazel.snow.2.0: Footprints in the snow. I'm reading them. One of them is yours.
dlg.hazel.snow.3.0: Snowfall, tea, and a book I'm not ready to finish. That's all I want.
dlg.hazel.wind.1.0: The wind turns pages without permission. I keep the windows shut. (The page I was on is gone.)
dlg.hazel.wind.2.0: A windy day. The shutters talk. I've begun to answer.
dlg.hazel.wind.3.0: Wind knocks the almanac off its shelf twice an hour. I stop picking it up on principle.
dlg.hazel.morning.1.0: Morning. I'm up early with the dust. We get along.
dlg.hazel.morning.2.0: Before opening, the library is just a room full of held breath.
dlg.hazel.morning.3.0: Mornings are for shelving and tea. In that order. (Mostly.)
dlg.hazel.midday.1.0: Midday. The library is at its busiest, which means three people and a draft.
dlg.hazel.midday.2.0: Afternoons I answer questions I wasn't asked, quietly, in my head.
dlg.hazel.midday.3.0: The light moves across the stacks all afternoon. I follow it with a feather duster.
dlg.hazel.evening.1.0: Evening. The library empties and the books relax.
dlg.hazel.evening.2.0: Closing soon. I give everyone a long look, so they hurry up and a short one, so they come back.
dlg.hazel.evening.3.0: Evening. The best time to read, and the worst time to be reminded of it.
dlg.hazel.late.1.0: It's late. I read in the kind of silence that has a color.
dlg.hazel.late.2.0: Late hours. I leave a lamp lit for anyone still walking home.
dlg.hazel.late.3.0: I should be asleep. The book disagrees.
dlg.hazel.here.1.0: Please don't dog-ear anything. I'll know. (I always know.)
dlg.hazel.here.2.0: The returns box is sticky. Nobody knows why. I've stopped asking.
dlg.hazel.here.3.0: The oldest book here is overdue by forty-one years. (I'm not counting.) (It's forty-one.)
dlg.hazel.fr.1.0: You return books early. I've told Ione. She wants to frame it.
dlg.hazel.fr.2.0: I've started to look up when the door opens. (Don't read into it.)
dlg.hazel.fr.3.0: You don't fill the silence. I appreciate that. I appreciate very little, so this is a lot.
dlg.hazel.fr.4.0: I put your name in the margin of a mystery novel. As the prime suspect. (Affectionately.)
dlg.hazel.fr.5.0: There's a chair in the nook I don't offer to anyone. It's open.
dlg.hazel.fr.6.0: I recommended a book to you without thinking. That's new.
dlg.hazel.fr.7.0: Wren asked how I know you. I said you borrowed a book once and gave it back. She nodded gravely.
dlg.hazel.fr.8.0: Someone left a seed packet in the poetry section. I planted it. It might be you.
dlg.hazel.cl.1.0: I talk more when you're around. I've counted. It's up forty percent.
dlg.hazel.cl.2.0: Ione says I hum when you visit. (I don't.) (I might.)
dlg.hazel.cl.3.0: I used to hide in the stacks when the door opened. Now I just shelve slowly.
dlg.hazel.cl.4.0: You make quiet feel like company. It's a very good trick.
dlg.hazel.cl.5.0: I keep a notebook of things I'd like to tell you. It has a table of contents.
dlg.hazel.cl.6.0: I wrote your name in the almanac. Under good weather.
dlg.hazel.cl.7.0: Please stop being this easy to talk to. I have a reputation for avoiding it.
dlg.hazel.cl.8.0: There are three people I'd trust with a bookmark. You're two of them.
dlg.hazel.co.1.0: I've read a lot of stories. Yours is the one I'd like to reread.
dlg.hazel.co.2.0: The library is quieter when you leave. Not worse. Just quieter.
dlg.hazel.co.3.0: I used to think I preferred books to people. I prefer you, with a book.
dlg.hazel.co.4.0: There's a shelf I keep for you. It's growing in a way I find alarming.
dlg.hazel.co.5.0: If I wrote your biography, I'd get the first line right and then wander off into footnotes.
dlg.hazel.co.6.0: You listen to me read. It still takes courage. It takes less every time.
dlg.hazel.co.7.0: I used to count the days until the library closed. Now I count the days until you open the door.
dlg.hazel.co.8.0: A person can be a favorite book. I'd put you on the nightstand.
dlg.hazel.lonely.1.0: It's been quiet. I read a whole book and had no one to tell. (It was good.)
dlg.hazel.lonely.2.0: I rehearsed things to say to you, and used none. (The rehearsals were better.)
dlg.hazel.tired.1.0: I stayed up with a book. It stayed up with me. We both regret it.
dlg.hazel.tired.2.0: Please speak slowly. My thoughts are still putting their shoes on.
dlg.hazel.delighted.1.0: I finished a book today. A good one. (I'm still holding it. I may not let go.)
dlg.hazel.delighted.2.0: Today is a very good day. I wrote it down so I'd believe it.
dlg.hazel.mischief.1.0: I hid a joke in the card catalog. Someone will find it. It will be you.
dlg.hazel.mischief.2.0: I've shelved your favorite book under 'Romance'. You can thank me or not.
dlg.hazel.worried.1.0: I've read the same page five times. It's not the page.
dlg.hazel.farm.1.0: I hear your crops are thriving. I read about farming for a week. I was not prepared for the mud.
dlg.hazel.farm.2.0: There's a book about a man who grew a hundred turnips and learned nothing. I'll hold it for you.
dlg.hazel.farm.3.0: Animals now. There's a very sad novel about a goat. I'll set it aside. (It has a happy ending. Probably.)
dlg.hazel.farm.4.0: Do your animals read? I ask for the shelves.
dlg.hazel.fest.1.0: A festival soon. I'll stand at the edge of it with a book. It's a plan.
dlg.hazel.fest.2.0: Ione says I should go to the festival. I said I'd think about it. I've thought about it.
dlg.hazel.fest.3.0: Festival today. I'm going for an hour. Possibly. Don't tell Ione.
dlg.hazel.bday.1.0: My birthday is soon. I'd like it to be quiet. I'd like it to be a tiny bit not quiet.
dlg.hazel.bday.2.0: Three days to my birthday. I've told no one. Ione has told everyone.
dlg.hazel.bday.3.0: It's my birthday. I'd like a quiet cake and no singing. (A little singing.)
dlg.hazel.bday.4.0: Ione's birthday is near. I wrote her a poem. Please don't ask to see it.
dlg.hazel.bday.5.0: Wren's birthday is close. She's already hinting. I'm bringing a very small book and a very large apology.
dlg.hazel.rare.1.0: I read the last chapter first. (Don't tell Ione.) (She knows.)
dlg.hazel.rare.2.0: There are three kinds of people: those who dog-ear, those who don't, and me, sharpening a pencil.
dlg.hazel.rare.3.0: Every book is a door. Most are quiet doors. You, I think, are a window.
dlg.hazel.rare.4.0: (She laughs, out loud, and covers her mouth.) That was not an aside. That was a joke. I made a joke.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.forage.blackberr: Blackberries. (She holds them very carefully.) I'll save them for the book I'm saving for them.
A strawberry. Perfectly red. I'll stain a bookmark and call it art.
A berry tart. You baked, or bought, or conspired. Either way, I'm going to eat it slowly, with a novel.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.forage.elderflow: Elderflower. Smells like the last page of a good summer. Thank you.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.crop.cauliflower: A cauliflower. That's... unexpected. (It's lovely.) (It's very big.)
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.artisan.jam.0: Jam. For toast, for tea, or for the bookmark that I will certainly ruin.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.resource.stone.0: A stone. It's quite heavy. (She sets it gently on the returns desk.) I'll use it as a bookend.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.resource.slime.0: Slime. I'm going to go stand very still for a moment. Thank you. (I'm grateful. Truly.)
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.resource.bat_win: A bat wing. (She flinches.) I'm going to put it in a box and pretend it's a very long bookmark.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.cat.Fish.0: A fish. It's looking at me. (She sets it down very gently on a sheet of paper.) Thank you. I think.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.resource.wood.0: A log. (Her eyes go wide.) I'll... shelve it under 'Nature'. Thank you.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.resource.coal.0: Coal. It's very dark. It looks like the last page of a sad novel. I'll take it.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.resource.bone.0: A bone. (A very long pause.) I'm going to label it and put it in a drawer. Thank you.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.product.egg.0: An egg. Fragile, full of potential, and slightly intimidating. I'll hold it until I understand it.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.product.milk.0: Milk. Warm milk is for people who stay up reading. (She looks at you, gently.) You know me too well.
A seashell. I'll hold it to my ear. (She does.) It says 'shh'. We get along.
A mushroom. (She takes it with two fingers.) It has such a calm face. I'll keep it on the sill.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.crop.parsnip.0: A parsnip. I have no notes. I'll treasure it.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.crop.pumpkin.0: A pumpkin. It's the size of a small, patient dog. I don't know where to put it. Thank you.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.artisan.wine.0: Wine. I'll save it for a day I finish a very hard book. (Or an easy one. I'm flexible.)
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.crop.hops.0: Hops. They're very green. I'll press one in the dictionary under 'H'.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.food.salad.0: A salad. A thoughtful, leafy thing. Thank you. I'll read while I eat it.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.item.crop.corn.0: Corn. It's a book of corn. I'll just look at it for a bit. Thank you.
dlg.npc.hazel.gift.repeat.0: Another one. (She smiles into her sleeve.) You're very consistent. It's one of my favorite things.
dlg.wren.spring.1.0: First warm night and every farmer wants a cider and an alibi for the mud.
dlg.wren.spring.2.0: Spring cleaning. I found a coin, two spoons, and a sock that belongs to Felix. Don't ask.
dlg.wren.spring.3.0: I open the windows in spring and the whole bar smells like rain. Cheaper than perfume.
dlg.wren.spring.4.0: Everyone plants too much in spring. Come summer they'll all be giving me turnips.
dlg.wren.spring.5.0: New season, new menu. Same soup. I just rename it.
dlg.wren.spring.6.0: Every spring I tell myself I'll learn to cook. Every spring the stove disagrees.
dlg.wren.summer.1.0: Summer nights run long. I pour slow. Slow is the whole trick.
dlg.wren.summer.2.0: The cider is cold, the fiddle is loud, and the fire is out. Finally, a fair fight.
dlg.wren.summer.3.0: Everyone's sunburned. I keep a bowl of cold pickles by the door. It's practically medicine.
dlg.wren.summer.4.0: Felix comes in smelling of fish and glowing with pride. I seat him by the door.
dlg.wren.summer.5.0: Warm evenings make people honest. Honest people tip well, or confess. Either one pays.
dlg.wren.summer.6.0: Between us, I count the fireflies from the back step. Forty-one last night.
dlg.wren.fall.1.0: Harvest season. Every farmer arrives with a story and a bruise, and the bruise is usually a pumpkin.
dlg.wren.fall.2.0: The first cold night, the whole village remembers I own a fireplace.
dlg.wren.fall.3.0: Marcus swears his barn is haunted. It's raccoons. I keep telling him it's the ghost of a raccoon.
dlg.wren.fall.4.0: I put cinnamon in everything this month. Nobody complains. Nobody can tell.
dlg.wren.fall.5.0: Leaves on the roof, rain on the leaves, a cider in my hand. This is the one.
dlg.wren.fall.6.0: My birthday's in fall. I tell everyone it's a rumor. It is not a rumor.
dlg.wren.winter.1.0: Winter, and the fire does half my work. I pour and I nod. That's the job.
dlg.wren.winter.2.0: The whole village is in here by four, steaming like soup.
dlg.wren.winter.3.0: I hang a lantern in the window when it snows. Anyone passing knows there's a seat.
dlg.wren.winter.4.0: Spiced cider all month. I stir it with a spoon I've never washed. Tradition.
dlg.wren.winter.5.0: Long nights, short tempers, and a very good stove. I'm fond of all three.
dlg.wren.winter.6.0: The packed bag under my bar has never been warmer. It's right by the stove.
dlg.wren.mon.1.0: Monday. Everyone's tired, and I'm only awake on principle.
dlg.wren.mon.2.0: Mondays are slow. I use them to rehearse stories for Fridays.
dlg.wren.tue.1.0: Tuesday's my day off. I spend it in a hammock, listening to rumors blow past.
dlg.wren.tue.2.0: The saloon's shut on Tuesdays. Don't tell me what I'm missing. I'll make it up.
dlg.wren.wed.1.0: Wednesday, the quietest night. I get my best material from the quiet.
dlg.wren.wed.2.0: Midweek. Everyone's done pretending they're organized.
dlg.wren.thu.1.0: Thursday, and the whole room's gearing up for the weekend. I can smell the ambition.
dlg.wren.thu.2.0: Piper does her new songs on Thursdays. Some of them even end.
dlg.wren.fri.1.0: Friday! The good stool's reserved. For anyone but Felix.
dlg.wren.fri.2.0: Friday night, the saloon sings. Not well. Enthusiastically.
dlg.wren.sat.1.0: Saturday, packed to the rafters. I pour with both hands.
dlg.wren.sat.2.0: Saturday night, between us, is where all the good rumors are born.
dlg.wren.sun.1.0: Sunday. Gentle crowd, gentle cider, gentle regret about Saturday.
dlg.wren.sun.2.0: Sunday afternoons I let the fire burn down and read people's moods instead.
dlg.wren.sunny.1.0: A bright day means a thin crowd. Everyone's outside pretending they enjoy it.
dlg.wren.sunny.2.0: Sunny out. The cider tastes better in the shade, I promise.
dlg.wren.sunny.3.0: Sunlight on the bar, dust in the air. It's like a very small stage.
dlg.wren.rain.3.0: Rain tapping the window and a full house inside. That's a good night's math.
dlg.wren.rain.4.0: Everyone comes in wet and apologizing. I hand out towels and opinions.
dlg.wren.storm.1.0: A storm like this and every story gets taller. By midnight it's a hurricane.
dlg.wren.storm.2.0: Thunder, and the whole room goes quiet. I pour a little slower for the drama.
dlg.wren.storm.3.0: I keep the lanterns lit in a storm. People find the door by habit.
dlg.wren.snow.1.0: Snow. Everyone walks in stamping and smiling like they've discovered fire.
dlg.wren.snow.2.0: First snow, and the saloon's the warmest room in Wetherell. I'd frame this if I could.
dlg.wren.snow.3.0: Between us, I love when the road disappears. Nobody leaves early.
dlg.wren.wind.1.0: The wind's got opinions today. The door has been arguing back since noon.
dlg.wren.wind.2.0: A windy day, and all the rumors get blown in, fully dressed.
dlg.wren.wind.3.0: Wind like this rattles the glasses. I take it as applause.
dlg.wren.morning.1.0: Morning? I'm barely a person before noon. Ask me again with coffee.
dlg.wren.morning.2.0: I don't open till noon. Mornings are for sweeping and sulking.
dlg.wren.morning.3.0: This early, the saloon is just a quiet room full of chairs thinking about themselves.
dlg.wren.afternoon.1.0: Slow afternoon. The calm before the clinking.
dlg.wren.afternoon.2.0: I polish the glasses at this hour. It's the only honest work I do.
dlg.wren.afternoon.3.0: Afternoons are for rumors that haven't been improved yet. Come back tonight.
dlg.wren.evening.1.0: Here comes the evening crowd. Brace yourself. Smile. Pour.
dlg.wren.evening.2.0: Lanterns on, fire up, stories warming. This is my favorite hour.
dlg.wren.evening.3.0: Evenings are when the village remembers it likes itself.
dlg.wren.late.1.0: Late. The honest hour. People say true things after nine and blame the cider.
dlg.wren.late.2.0: The fire's low and the stories are lower. I love it.
dlg.wren.late.3.0: Last call is a suggestion. Closing is a negotiation.
dlg.wren.here.1.0: Welcome to my kingdom. Population: me, a stove, and some chairs.
dlg.wren.here.2.0: See that scorch mark? Felix, a flaming dessert, and a bet. I'm still billing him.
dlg.wren.here.3.0: Every dent in this bar is a story. That one's the pickle incident. We don't discuss it.
dlg.wren.fr.1.0: You know where I keep the good napkins. That's real trust.
dlg.wren.fr.2.0: I've started saving you the first pour. Don't make it weird.
dlg.wren.fr.3.0: You listen without trying to top my story. Do you know how rare that is?
dlg.wren.fr.4.0: Careful. You laugh at my jokes and I'll start telling more of them.
dlg.wren.fr.5.0: Piper says you have a good face for gossip. I took it as a compliment.
dlg.wren.fr.6.0: Sit, sit. I've got a rumor with your name on it. Kidding. Mostly.
dlg.wren.fr.7.0: Tilda says you're the best thing to happen to the village. I told her to get in line.
dlg.wren.fr.8.0: The stool by the fire has a dip in it now. It's shaped like you.
dlg.wren.cl.1.0: I told a story about you last night. It was all true. That's how I know I like you.
dlg.wren.cl.2.0: I stopped improving my stories about you. Didn't need to.
dlg.wren.cl.3.0: When you walk in, the room changes. Between us, I notice.
dlg.wren.cl.4.0: You're the only one who asks how I am and waits for the answer.
dlg.wren.cl.5.0: I almost left this village once. Then you showed up and ruined it. Thank you.
dlg.wren.cl.6.0: I keep a tab for everyone. Yours has a drawing of a pie on it. It's a long story.
dlg.wren.cl.7.0: I'd tell you a secret, but you'd put it on a sign and ruin my reputation.
dlg.wren.cl.8.0: Some friends I pour for. You, I pour with.
dlg.wren.co.1.0: People come here for the cider. Some for the stories. You, I think, came for me.
dlg.wren.co.2.0: Do you know what the best part of my job is now? Watching you walk in.
dlg.wren.co.3.0: I don't need to embellish with you. That's a first. It scares me. I like it.
dlg.wren.co.4.0: This place is a lot of noise, and a lot of faces. You're the one I look for.
dlg.wren.co.5.0: If I wrote a book, you'd be the only chapter nobody believes.
dlg.wren.co.6.0: The stool's yours. The fire's yours. The soup, we'll leave to the professionals.
dlg.wren.co.7.0: Between us, I've stopped checking whether the bag is still under the bar.
dlg.wren.co.8.0: Some people make a place feel like a stage. You made mine feel like home.
dlg.wren.lonely.1.0: You were gone a while. I told the chairs. They didn't care.
dlg.wren.lonely.2.0: Quiet week. I rehearsed three speeches for you and used none. Sit down.
dlg.wren.tired.1.0: I'm running on cider and spite. Nobody tell Tilda.
dlg.wren.tired.2.0: Long night. If I fall asleep mid-story, wake me for the ending.
dlg.wren.delighted.1.0: Good day! Good, good day. I could pour for the whole village and forget to charge.
dlg.wren.delighted.2.0: Have you ever had a day where everything works? Me neither. Today's the first.
dlg.wren.mischief.1.0: I've got a rumor and no evidence. The best kind.
dlg.wren.mischief.2.0: Between us, I've been telling people you're a duke. Play along.
dlg.wren.worried.1.0: Nothing's wrong. I just keep counting the chairs. They keep coming up the same.
dlg.wren.farm.1.0: I hear you've got a real field going. Everyone's saying so. I may have started it.
dlg.wren.farm.2.0: When you've got tomatoes, I want the first crate. My kitchen is a battlefield of sad ones.
dlg.wren.farm.3.0: A real farm now, with animals. Do they gossip? They look the type.
dlg.wren.farm.4.0: Next you'll tell me the chickens have names. They do? Of course they do.
dlg.wren.fest.1.0: Festival soon. I'm stocking up on cider and excuses.
dlg.wren.fest.2.0: Festival's almost here. The whole village is about to be in one place. I love it.
dlg.wren.fest.3.0: It's festival day! Be good. Be loud. Come back and tell me everything.
dlg.wren.bday.1.0: My birthday is close. I'm not hinting. I'm lighting a very small flare.
dlg.wren.bday.2.0: Three days till I'm one year wiser and no less nosy.
dlg.wren.bday.3.0: It's my birthday! Drinks are on me. Mostly. Some are on Felix.
dlg.wren.bday.4.0: Piper's birthday's around the corner. I'm planning a surprise. She'll find out by supper.
dlg.wren.bday.5.0: Bram's birthday's coming. I bet him I'd get four words out of him. He's in for a rough day.
dlg.wren.rare.1.0: I never repeat gossip. I improve it.
dlg.wren.rare.2.0: If the walls could talk, I'd charge them rent.
dlg.wren.rare.3.0: Between us: every good story in this room started with somebody nervous at the door.
dlg.wren.rare.4.0: Want to know the secret to a good story? Make sure someone's listening. You do.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.artisan.wine.0: Is this the good vintage? Oh, you terrible, wonderful enabler. Between us, I'll save it for a night I deserve.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.crop.hops.0: Hops! You've got the touch. I could brew a song out of these.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.artisan.pickles.0: Pickles! My favorite bar food and my favorite excuse. You know me.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.artisan.juice.0: Juice! For the nights I'm trying to behave. Thank you. It'll last until Thursday.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.crop.tomato.0: A tomato. I'll put it in the soup and call it mine.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.crop.pepper.0: A pepper. Now the soup has a personality. Thank you.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.forage.clam.0: A clam. Hm. I once served a clam. We lost two customers and a dog.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.food.bean_stew.0: Bean stew? Oh, that's thoughtful. I make forty gallons a week. I'll treat it as a mirror.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.resource.slime.0: Slime. For me. A gift from the heart, surely, because it's definitely not from the kitchen.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.cat.Fish.0: A fish! Fresh? Excellent. Felix will want to know where you got it, and then he'll want it back.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.resource.stone.0: A rock. Between us, I've been looking for one to prop the back door. You have a gift for it.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.resource.wood.0: A log. I'll use it. Or I'll tell people it's a sculpture. Either way, thank you.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.resource.coal.0: Coal. For the stove, or for my enemies' stockings. Thank you.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.resource.bone.0: A bone. Well. This'll make a fine conversation piece, and an even finer silence.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.resource.bat_wing: A bat wing. I'm going to put it on the wall and tell everyone it's a dragon's. Thank you.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.product.egg.0: An egg! Everything starts with one. Including omelets, lawsuits, and rumors.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.product.milk.0: Milk? You think I need calming? Fine. Between us, I do.
A dandelion. Sweet. Do I make a wish? Don't answer.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.forage.seashell.0: A seashell. Hold it to my ear? It says Felix owes me money.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.forage.mushroom.0: A mushroom. You trust me not to cook it. I appreciate that. I'll set it on the windowsill and admire it.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.crop.parsnip.0: A parsnip. The most honest vegetable. I'll hang it by the door for luck.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.crop.pumpkin.0: A pumpkin! Wonderful. I'll carve it into a very rude face and put it by Marcus's door.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.crop.corn.0: Corn. Hm. Corn at a bar. I see where this is going, and I like it.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.item.food.salad.0: A salad. For me? That's either a kindness or a very sharp hint. I'll eat it.
dlg.npc.wren.gift.repeat.0: Another one? You're spoiling me, and I've made my peace with it.
event.wren_heart4.setup: Don't sit yet. I'm trying something new, and I need a witness.
event.wren_heart4.prank: Ladies and gentlemen: the worst song ever written!
event.wren_heart4.reaction: Terrible, wasn't it? I wrote it in the bath. The bath had notes.
event.wren_heart6.intro: Come into the back. I'm testing a stew, and I trust nobody else's tongue.
event.wren_heart6.after: Remember this one. If it goes wrong, I'll deny I ever made it.
event.wren_heart8.intro: Close the door behind you. No, the other one. Yes. Sit.
event.wren_heart8.after: Thank you for letting me say it out loud. It weighs less now.
event.wren_heart10.intro: Tonight's a performance. One song, one listener. I picked you.
event.wren_heart10.outro: {if choice:wren.bag.go}I'm not leaving yet. But I wrote the map into the second verse.{else}{if choice:wren.bag.stay}I wrote the stay into the chorus. You'll hear it.{else}I wrote the quiet part for you. You'll know which.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_friend.intro: Friday means bingo. Not numbers. Gossip. Come and cross something off.
event.wren_friend.doing: Someone's cat is in love with the postal cart. I'm marking it.
event.wren_friend.wrap: No bingo today. Only a full house of nonsense. Wonderful.
event.hazel_heart4.intro: I'd like to swap something. (A book for a book.) Is that odd?
event.hazel_heart4.after: Thank you. (I'll look after it.) I always do.
event.hazel_heart6.intro: Could you come to the back? (There's something I don't say out loud.)
event.hazel_heart6.after: Thank you for not laughing. (I checked your face.) It stayed kind.
event.hazel_heart8.intro: Would you hear a thing I wrote? (Only one of you. Just one.)
event.hazel_heart8.after: I'll read it properly, one day. (To more than one.)
event.hazel_heart10.intro: I'll read for you. (Just you. The shelves don't count.)
event.hazel_heart10.outro: {if choice:hazel.rehearsal.critique}I cut the middle. (You were right.) Thank you.{else}I kept the lamp. (And you.) Thank you.{/if}
event.hazel_friend.ask: Do you have blackberries? (I'm baking a peace offering for an overdue book.)
event.hazel_friend.success: Perfect. (He'll forgive me. Or at least eat.) Thank you.
event.hazel_friend.fallback: Come back with blackberries? (It's a small crisis. A quiet one.)
event.bram_heart4.intro: Hm. Come here. I need a second pair of hands.
event.bram_heart4.after: Hm. Good enough. Better than good.
event.bram_heart6.intro: Hm. Sit. I've got something to say. It'll be long for me.
event.bram_heart6.after: Hm. That's all of it. Don't ask me to repeat it.
event.bram_heart8.intro: Hm. Juno made something. I want you to look at it. Tell me true.
event.bram_heart8.after: Hm. Thanks. I'll tell her. Maybe.
event.bram_heart10.intro: Hm. I made you something. Don't speak. Just take it.
event.bram_heart10.give: Gold. Soft. Not for work. For you. Hm.
event.bram_heart10.thanks: {if choice:bram.juno.ask}You asked what I see. I see you. Hm.{else}Hm. It's not much. It's all I could say.{/if}
event.bram_friend.intro: Hm. Marcus is closed. We sit. Come on.
event.bram_friend.doing: Hm. Good bench. Good silence. Don't spoil it.
event.bram_friend.wrap: Hm. That was nice. Don't tell anyone.
dlg.wren.openmic.0: Well? Be honest. A performer needs one honest face in the crowd.
dlg.wren.openmic.r0: Oh, I could live on that. Do it again, but louder.
dlg.wren.openmic.r1: A heckler! At last I'm somebody. I'll put you in the second verse.
dlg.wren.openmic.r2: Ha! Fair. I'd hide too. Come out, though. The second verse is better.
dlg.wren.kitchen.0: One more pinch of something. Pepper, cider, or leave it plain?
dlg.wren.kitchen.r0: Brave it is! If I weep, blame the pepper, not me.
dlg.wren.kitchen.r1: Cider. Sweet and a little sly. That's very you.
dlg.wren.kitchen.r2: Plain. Hm. You think it's already good? Nobody says that. I'm keeping you.
dlg.wren.bag.0: There's a bag under my bed. Packed since the day I arrived. I haven't opened it in years, and I haven't unpacked it either.
dlg.wren.bag.1: I came here to rest for a season. That was eight years ago. Tell me: should I go, stay, or just keep it under the bed?
dlg.wren.bag.r0: Go. Hm. You say it so plainly. I might. Someday. With a very good map.
dlg.wren.bag.r1: Stay. Oh. That's a nicer word than I expected.
dlg.wren.bag.r2: ...You didn't tell me what to do. That's the kindest thing anyone has done. Thank you.
dlg.hazel.swap.0: What would you swap? (I'm not choosing for you.)
dlg.hazel.swap.r0: Oh. (She holds it with both hands.) I'll read it twice.
dlg.hazel.swap.r1: A recipe. (A book without a spine.) I like that.
dlg.hazel.swap.r2: Thank you for saying so. (Most people pretend.) I'll pick something short.
dlg.hazel.hiding.0: I hide in the stacks when it's loud. (It's quieter between the books.) Is that strange?
dlg.hazel.hiding.r0: Pages turning, far away. (Someone else's thoughts, stored.) It's company.
dlg.hazel.hiding.r2: Ha. (A small one.) You're not wrong.
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.0: ...and so the lamp burned lower, and nobody minded. (That's the end.) What did you hear?
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r0: Lovely. (I'll hold on to that word.) Thank you.
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r1: The middle. (I knew it.) Thank you for saying so out loud.
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r2: The lamp is a bit much. (It was supposed to be.) I'll keep it.
dlg.bram.repair.0: Hm. The handle's cracked. Hold, hammer, or watch?
dlg.bram.repair.r2: Hm. Watching's a skill. Few have it.
dlg.bram.long.0: I worked alone a long time, and I decided I liked it, and I was wrong about that, and I'm saying so because you came in and sat down.
dlg.bram.long.r1: Hm. Glad. Hm. Yes. Me too.
dlg.bram.juno.0: She made a horseshoe. Crooked. She's proud. What do I say?
dlg.bram.juno.r0: Hm. Wonderful. It's crooked. Still wonderful.
dlg.bram.juno.r1: Ha. Hm. I'll tease her. Gently. With a nail.
dlg.bram.juno.r2: ...Hm. Me. When I started. That's what I see.
dlg.hazel.hiding.c0: Ask what she hears in the quiet.
dlg.hazel.hiding.c2: Joke about hiding in a book.
dlg.bram.juno.c2: Ask what he sees in it.
letter.wren_bday.subject: Someone has a birthday coming
letter.wren_bday.body: Between us, I do hate fuss. But if you were to bring something wrapped, I would pretend to be surprised. Don't say I asked. -- Wren
letter.wren_thanks.subject: A song for you
letter.wren_thanks.body: That terrible song? I'm keeping the second verse. It's yours now. Come hear the third one when it exists. -- Wren
letter.hazel_bday.subject: A note, very small
letter.hazel_bday.body: My birthday is soon. (I don't mind if it passes quietly.) A book would not be unwelcome. -- Hazel
letter.hazel_thanks.subject: About the swap
letter.hazel_thanks.body: I read it twice. (As promised.) Come by when you have an opinion. -- Hazel
letter.bram_bday.subject: Hm
letter.bram_bday.body: Birthday soon. No fuss. Copper would be fine. -- Bram
letter.bram_thanks.subject: Handle
letter.bram_thanks.body: Handle held. Good work. Come by. -- Bram
dlg.react.wren.spring.d.0: Spring! The whole village smells like mud and good intentions. I love it. Don't tell the mud.
dlg.react.wren.winter.d.0: First snow, and my stove has already started a feud with the draft. Come in. Pick a side.
dlg.react.wren.harvest.d.0: I heard you harvested something! Everyone's talking. Mostly me. Show me what grew.
dlg.react.wren.coins.d.0: A little bird told me you found coins. The bird was me. I follow everything.
dlg.react.hazel.spring.d.0: The windows are open. (The pages like it.) Spring smells like paper.
dlg.react.hazel.winter.d.0: Snow. (The library is the warmest place in town.) Stay as long as you like.
dlg.react.hazel.harvest.d.0: You grew something. (I'm told that's a skill.) I'd like to read about it.
dlg.react.hazel.wren.d.0: I heard a song from the saloon. (Through three walls.) It was terrible. I think she knew.
dlg.react.bram.spring.d.0: Hm. Spring. Plows are coming. Bring yours early.
dlg.react.bram.winter.d.0: Hm. Snow. Forge is warm. Sit if you like.
dlg.react.bram.harvest.d.0: Hm. First harvest. Good. Your hoe held up. I noticed.
dlg.react.bram.wren.d.0: Hm. Wren sang. I heard. Don't tell her I listened.
dlg.wren.pie.1.0: Marcus and Odalys are not speaking over a pie. I'm running a betting pool. Don't tell them.
dlg.wren.pie.2.0: The pie feud's day nine. The pie is still on the windowsill. Nobody dares touch it.
dlg.wren.notes.1.0: Someone's leaving notes on doors. "Nice shoes," one said. I'm flattered. I wasn't wearing shoes.
dlg.wren.notes.2.0: I found a note that only said "Hello." It's the nicest thing that's happened this week.
dlg.hazel.pie.1.0: A pie, two neighbors. (I'm cataloguing the feud under "Domestic.") Nobody asked.
dlg.hazel.pie.2.0: The pie has gone stale. (The feud hasn't.) I find that instructive.
dlg.hazel.notes.1.0: Someone slipped a note into a book. (It said "Good choice.") I'm not sure which book.
dlg.hazel.notes.2.0: I think the notes are kind. (I'm trying not to look for the writer.) Looking spoils it.
dlg.bram.pie.1.0: Hm. Pie feud. Two fools, one crust. I'd fix it with a hammer.
dlg.bram.pie.2.0: Hm. Both sides asked me to make a pie plate. I made one. Gave it to Juno.
dlg.bram.notes.1.0: Hm. A note on my anvil. It said "Nice work." Hm. I read it twice.
dlg.bram.notes.2.0: Hm. I don't know who writes the notes. I'd like to say thanks.
dlg.wren.bark.1.0: Fresh cider, fresh gossip, fresh start every Tuesday!
dlg.wren.bark.2.0: Someone owes me a rhyme for "turnip".
dlg.wren.bark.3.0: I'm not eavesdropping. The walls are just very talkative.
dlg.wren.bark.4.0: Day four of asking Bram for four words. Progress: "Hm."
dlg.wren.bark.5.0: Hazel borrowed my notebook. I hope she returns the gossip.
dlg.wren.bark.6.0: If a story's too good, I only improve it slightly.
dlg.wren.bark.7.0: Does anyone else hear a lute? No? Just me?
dlg.wren.bark.8.0: I'm writing a song about weather. It's mostly sighing.
dlg.wren.bark.rain.1.0: Rain on the roof. Best band in the village.
dlg.wren.bark.rain.2.0: Drip, drip, drip. I can't rhyme this one.
dlg.wren.bark.storm.1.0: That thunder has terrible timing. I admire it.
dlg.wren.bark.snow.1.0: Snow! Everything looks like it's keeping a secret.
dlg.wren.bark.spring.1.0: Spring! Everyone's hopeful and slightly muddy. My favorite crowd.
dlg.wren.bark.summer.1.0: Hot day. Cold cider. Honest math.
dlg.wren.bark.fall.1.0: Fall smells like cinnamon and other people's secrets.
dlg.wren.bark.winter.1.0: Winter: the season of stew and over-sharing.
dlg.wren.bark.morning.1.0: Too early for jokes. I'll do a mild pun.
dlg.wren.bark.evening.1.0: Evening crowd's in. Everyone has a story. Some are even true.
dlg.wren.bark.here.1.0: Sit anywhere. Except Felix's stool. It remembers him.
dlg.wren.bark.here.2.0: House rule: no sad songs before the second cider.
dlg.wren.bark.tue.1.0: Tuesday. My day off, my favorite hammock.
dlg.wren.bark.fri.1.0: Friday! Gossip bingo, anyone? Free pencil!
dlg.wren.bark.rare.1.0: I'm going to be famous. Eventually. Maybe posthumously.
dlg.wren.bark.rare.2.0: Whoever's reading this: you're doing better than you think.
dlg.hazel.bark.1.0: (Quietly.) Please. This is a library. A small one.
dlg.hazel.bark.2.0: I've misplaced a bookmark. (It's in a book.) Somewhere.
dlg.hazel.bark.3.0: Wren borrowed a pencil. (That's three weeks ago.)
dlg.hazel.bark.4.0: (Reading.) Hm. The ending is better than the middle.
dlg.hazel.bark.5.0: The index is out of order. (It's me. I did it.)
dlg.hazel.bark.6.0: Overdue books come back smelling of cider. (I won't ask.)
dlg.hazel.bark.7.0: I like this quiet. (It has good margins.)
dlg.hazel.bark.8.0: Bram returned a book early. (Again.) I'm suspicious.
dlg.hazel.bark.rain.1.0: Rain on the window. (Best soundtrack for a chapter.)
dlg.hazel.bark.rain.2.0: The roof ticks in the rain. (Like a slow clock.)
dlg.hazel.bark.storm.1.0: (Reading by candle.) Storms improve every sentence.
dlg.hazel.bark.snow.1.0: Snow. (Everything is a footnote to it.)
dlg.hazel.bark.spring.1.0: Windows open. (Pages turning on their own.)
dlg.hazel.bark.summer.1.0: Warm. (The books are drowsy.) So am I.
dlg.hazel.bark.fall.1.0: Fall is the season for long sentences.
dlg.hazel.bark.winter.1.0: Winter. (Tea, a blanket, a thick book.)
dlg.hazel.bark.evening.1.0: Almost closing. (One more chapter. Always one more.)
dlg.hazel.bark.here.1.0: Take your time. (Not too much of mine.)
dlg.hazel.bark.here.2.0: The cat section is on the left. (There isn't a cat.)
dlg.hazel.bark.sat.1.0: Saturday. (The village is loud. I read louder.)
dlg.hazel.bark.wed.1.0: Wednesday. (Nothing happens on Wednesdays.) I like that.
dlg.hazel.bark.rare.1.0: I'm writing a book about bookmarks. (It's a very short book.)
dlg.hazel.bark.rare.2.0: Someone left a note in a book. (It said, "Good choice.")
dlg.bram.bark.3.0: Careful. It's hot. It's always hot.
dlg.bram.bark.4.0: Wren talks. I listen. It's a system.
dlg.bram.bark.5.0: Hm. Juno labeled the tongs again.
dlg.bram.bark.6.0: Someone put a rubber chicken on the anvil. Hm.
dlg.bram.bark.7.0: Returned Hazel's book. Early. She stared.
dlg.bram.bark.rain.1.0: Rain. Roof's holding. Fire's holding. Good.
dlg.bram.bark.wind.1.0: Wind blows the ash around. Hm.
dlg.bram.bark.winter.1.0: Winter. The best seat is the forge.
dlg.bram.bark.here.2.0: Hm. Mind the floor. It has opinions.
dlg.bram.bark.rare.2.0: A good tool. A good friend. Both take time.
